The test image shows a close-up of a soybean **leaf** with:
- Prominent yellow/chlorotic tissue surrounding a dark brown-black lesion
- The central lesion is nearly black, somewhat circular
- Macro shot showing leaf cell texture and white trichomes
- Mottled yellow-green pattern around the lesion

This affects a **leaf**. Key candidates: Frogeye leaf spot, Septoria brown spot, Bacterial Blight, Phyllosticta leaf spot.

The prominent dark lesion surrounded by chlorotic tissue makes Frogeye leaf spot a strong candidate. Let me check one reference.

The frogeye reference shows small circular lesions on a **green** leaf with tissue falling out — not matching the test image at all.

The test image has:
- Heavily chlorotic/yellow leaf (extensive yellowing)
- A very dark (near-black), somewhat irregular lesion
- The yellowing extends well beyond the necrotic area

This matches **Septoria brown spot** best: dark brown irregular lesions where "leaf yellowing expands far beyond the necrotic region," with lesions coalescing and causing lower canopy yellowing. The extensive chlorosis surrounding a dark central lesion is characteristic.
